source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"An improvement in the client's overall neurological function reflected by this particular assessment finding noted at the bedside","B":"A permanent, unchanging finding with fairly little possibility of any improvement occurring over the following days, weeks, or months","C":"Spinal shock, a temporary physiological response following spinal cord injury, distinct from the permanent injury itself, that may resolve over days to weeks","D":"A fairly ordinary finding generally considered unrelated to the client's underlying spinal cord injury itself in this scenario"}}
source_row.rationale: Spinal shock is a temporary physiological response following spinal cord injury, causing complete loss of motor/sensory function and absent reflexes below the injury level, distinct from the permanent structural injury itself; spinal shock may resolve over days to weeks, at which point the true extent of permanent neurological deficit can be better assessed.
source_row.source_detail: Distinguishing Spinal Shock from Permanent Injury
source_row.source_name: Consortium for Spinal Cord Medicine — Spinal Shock Recognition
